date_note: Date of the OM announcement as reported by Security.nl.
exec: The Dutch prosecution service has said it used covert network access and phone taps in a criminal pollution case against Tata Steel.
plain: The Dutch Public Prosecution Service says that in its criminal investigation of Tata Steel it covertly entered the company's digital network and tapped phones.

key_findings: The OM said that in its criminal investigation of Tata Steel it hacked the company's digital network and tapped phones.
It did not say how the network was entered; it is not known whether the hack produced evidence.
Tata Steel's lawyer, quoted by NOS, said wiretapping and hacking took place.

sources.name: Security.nl: Openbaar Ministerie hackte voor onderzoek bedrijfsnetwerk Tata Steel

summary: Security.nl reports that the Dutch Public Prosecution Service (OM) said on 20 November that in its criminal investigation of Tata Steel it covertly entered the company's digital network and tapped phones. The OM did not say how the network was entered. Tata Steel's lawyer, quoted by NOS, said wiretapping and hacking took place. Tata Steel is suspected of five criminal offences; the first pre-trial hearing was held in Amsterdam.
title: Dutch prosecutors say they hacked Tata Steel's corporate network in pollution investigation

validation.note: Single publisher (Security.nl) relaying the OM statement and NOS; originals not read.

review.note: Summary said five charges; Security.nl says suspected of five criminal offences; reworded. OM statement, date, lawyer quote match.
